audience: Finance users who plan a year's income and expenses and want to compare them with the actual General Ledger postings.
goal: Record a **ledger budget** in two stages: first create two **Budgetary Positions** that group General Ledger accounts (one for **income**, one for **expenses**), then create the **Budget** itself with a **planned amount** for each position, **confirm** it and open **Budgets Analysis**.
before: You can open the **Accounting** app, with its **Configuration**, **Accounting** and **Reporting** menus.
You know the General Ledger account codes to budget: here **41010010 SALES** and **41010050 SERVICE INCOME** for income, **51010010 COST OF GOODS SOLD** and **51050010 ELECTRICITY** for expenses.
You know the budget period (here **01/01/2028 – 31/12/2028**) and the planned amounts (**250,000,000** income, **−180,000,000** expenses).
outcome: Two budgetary positions exist: a revenue position and an operating-expense position, each grouping its accounts.
A budget for the year has two lines, one per position, and is **Confirmed**.
You have seen the budget in **Budgets Analysis**, where planned amounts are compared with practical (posted) amounts.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The red banner at the top ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases. Names carry a `[TEST]` tag and a random code, and the run **deletes everything it creates** (the positions and the budget) afterwards.

In the account picker, **once you tick an account Odoo hides the search box**. So the guide searches a short code prefix once (**41010** for income, **510** for expenses) and ticks both accounts from the same list. Searching for each account separately is not possible after the first tick.

On this database the **Budget** column on a budget line is **required**. It cannot be filled while the budget is unsaved, so **save the budget (header only) before you add lines**. The automated run does this; the lines then pick up the budget by themselves.

Do **not** press **Tab** after typing the last planned amount. In Odoo, Tab on the last cell of the last line starts a new, empty line, and Odoo then refuses to save ("You have to enter at least a budgetary position or analytic account on a budget line").
Planned amounts are signed: **income is positive, expenses are negative**, so that plan and actual are compared in the same direction.
The budget period is in 2028, so **Practical Amount** shows **0.0000** in the screenshots: nothing has been posted in that period yet.

phases.title: Create the income position
phases.summary: Open Budgetary Positions and group the revenue accounts.
phases.checkpoint: The **revenue position** is saved with **41010010 SALES** and **41010050 SERVICE INCOME**.

phases.title: Create the expense position
phases.summary: Do the same for the expense accounts.
phases.checkpoint: The **expense position** is saved with **51010010** and **51050010**. Both positions can now be reused by any budget.

phases.title: Create the budget
phases.summary: Name the budget, set its period and add a planned line for each position.
phases.checkpoint: The budget is saved with two lines: **+250,000,000** and **−180,000,000**.

phases.title: Confirm and analyse
phases.summary: Read the computed columns, confirm the budget and open the analysis.
phases.checkpoint: The budget is **Confirmed** and appears in **Budgets Analysis**.

glossary.meaning: A budget driven by General Ledger accounts (through budgetary positions) rather than by analytic accounts.
A named group of Chart of Accounts lines that the budget measures actual postings against.
The amount you plan for the period. Income is positive, expenses are negative.
What has actually been posted on the position's accounts inside the period.
The plan spread evenly over the period, up to today.
The ratio between the practical and the theoretical amount.
Moves the budget from Draft to Confirmed, so it is treated as an approved plan.
Income positions should hold Income or Other Income accounts; expense positions Expenses, Cost of Revenue or Depreciation. Never balance-sheet accounts.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen.
1.see: The Accounting app opens with its menu bar across the top.
1.why: A ledger budget is built in two stages: first the Budgetary Positions that group the General Ledger accounts, then the Budget itself that carries the planned amounts.

2.title: Open the Configuration menu
2.do: In the top menu bar, click **Configuration**.
2.see: A drop-down with the set-up entries.
2.why: Budgetary positions are set up under Configuration.

3.title: Open Budgetary Positions
3.where: Accounting app > Configuration > Management > Budgetary Positions
3.why: A position is a named basket of Chart of Accounts lines that the budget will measure actuals against.

4.title: Create the income position
actions: Click the **New** button at the top left.
4.why: You create the income side first.

5.title: Name the position
5.do: Type the name **FY2028 Revenue - Ledger Budget**.
5.see: The name appears in the form.
5.why: Name it so that both the period and the side of the profit and loss are obvious to the next user.

6.title: Add a line
6.do: Click **Add a line** to attach the revenue accounts.
6.where: Position form > Accounts > Add a line
6.see: The **Add: Accounts** window opens with a list of accounts.
6.why: The accounts you pick here are the ones the budget will measure.

7.title: Search for the revenue accounts
actions: Click the search box at the top of the window.
7.see: Your text appears in the search box.
7.why: A short prefix finds both revenue accounts at once.
7.warning: Only pick accounts whose type is **Income** or **Other Income**. A balance-sheet account makes the budget comparison meaningless.

8.title: Run the search
8.see: The list shows the matching accounts, including **41010010 SALES** and **41010050 SERVICE INCOME**.

9.title: Tick 41010010 SALES
actions: Tick its box on the left.
9.see: The row is highlighted and the top shows **1 selected**.
9.why: This is the first revenue account of the position.

10.title: The selection stays
10.do: Look at the **1 selected** counter at the top.
actions: Look at the top of the window.
10.see: **1 selected**. The search box is now hidden.
10.why: Once an account is ticked Odoo hides the search box, so you cannot search for the next account. Pick the next one from the same list.
10.warning: Do not click the **×** next to **1 selected**: it clears your selection.

11.title: Find 41010050 SERVICE INCOME
11.do: Find **41010050 SERVICE INCOME** in the same list.
11.see: The second revenue account is listed.
11.why: It is the second revenue account for this position.

12.title: Check the account
12.do: Check the row says **SERVICE INCOME** and the type is **Income**.
actions: Read the account name and type in the row.
12.why: Only Income-type accounts belong in a revenue position.

13.title: Tick 41010050 SERVICE INCOME
13.do: Tick the box on **41010050 SERVICE INCOME**.
actions: Tick the box on the left of the row.
13.why: Both revenue accounts are now chosen.

14.title: Select the accounts
14.see: The window closes and both accounts are listed in the position.
14.why: Both revenue accounts are pulled into the position.

15.title: Save the position
actions: Look at the top left, beside the position name.
15.see: The cloud icon disappears. The position is saved.
15.why: The revenue position now exists and can be reused by any budget.

16.title: Back to Budgetary Positions
actions: Click **Budgetary Positions** at the top left.
16.see: The list of positions, now with your revenue position.
16.why: The expense position is created in exactly the same way.

17.title: Create the expense position
17.why: This time for the expense side.

18.title: Name the position
18.see: The name appears in the form.
18.why: The name makes the side and the period obvious.

19.title: Add a line
19.where: Position form > Accounts > Add a line
actions: Click **Add a line** in the Accounts tab.

20.title: Search for the expense accounts
20.see: Your text appears in the search box.
20.why: A short prefix finds both expense accounts.
20.warning: Only accounts of type **Expenses, Cost of Revenue or Depreciation** belong in an expense position.

21.title: Run the search
21.see: The list shows the matching accounts.

22.title: Tick 51010010 COST OF GOODS SOLD
22.do: Tick the box on **51010010 COST OF GOODS SOLD**.
actions: Find the row **51010010 COST OF GOODS SOLD**.
22.see: The row is ticked and **1 selected** shows at the top.
22.why: The first expense account of the position.

23.title: The selection stays
actions: Look at the top of the window.
23.see: **1 selected**. The search box is hidden again.
23.why: As before, pick the next account from the same list.
23.warning: Do not click the **×** next to **1 selected**.

24.title: Find 51050010 ELECTRICITY
24.do: Find **51050010 ELECTRICITY** in the same list.
24.see: The second expense account is listed.
24.why: It is the second expense account.

25.title: Check the account
25.do: Check the row and its type.
actions: Read the account name and type.
25.why: Only expense-type accounts belong in this position.

26.title: Tick 51050010 ELECTRICITY
actions: Tick the box on the left of the row.

27.title: Select the accounts
27.see: The window closes and both accounts are listed in the position.
27.why: Both expense accounts are pulled into the position.

28.title: Save the position
28.why: Both budgetary positions now exist and can be reused by any future budget.

29.title: Open the Accounting menu
29.do: In the top menu bar, click **Accounting**.
29.see: A drop-down with the Accounting entries, including **Budgets**.
29.why: The budget record itself lives under Management here.

30.title: Open Budgets
30.why: This is where budgets are created.

31.title: Create the budget
31.why: You start the budget for the year.

32.title: Name the budget
32.see: The name appears at the top.
32.why: A clear name makes the budget easy to find.

33.title: Set the period start
33.do: Enter **01/01/2028** as the start of the period.

34.title: Set the period end
34.do: Enter **31/12/2028** as the end of the period.
34.why: Only journal items posted inside this window count as practical amounts.
34.tip: Now save the budget once, **before** adding lines: the line's **Budget** column is required and can only be filled once the budget is saved.

35.title: Add a line (income)
35.do: Click **Add a line** to enter the income side.
35.where: Budget form > Budget Lines > Add a line
35.see: A new line, with its dates already set to the budget period.
35.why: Each line is one position with its planned amount.

36.title: Choose the revenue position
36.do: In **Budgetary Position**, pick **FY2028 Revenue - Ledger Budget**.
actions: Click the revenue position in the list.
36.see: The position name appears in the line.
36.why: Leave **Analytic Account** empty: this is a ledger budget driven by General Ledger accounts, not by analytic distribution.
36.warning: Pick the **Revenue** position here and the **Operating Expenses** one on the second line. Mixing them up reverses the comparison.

37.title: Line start date
37.do: Enter **01/01/2028** as the line start date.
37.why: The line has its own period.

38.title: Line end date
38.do: Enter **31/12/2028** as the line end date.
38.why: The line covers the whole year.

39.title: Planned amount: income
actions: Do not press **Tab**; click elsewhere to finish.
39.why: Income is budgeted as a **positive** figure.
39.warning: Do not press **Tab** after the last amount. It starts a new, empty line and Odoo then refuses to save.

40.title: Add a line (expense)
40.do: Click **Add a line** again for the expense side.
40.where: Budget form > Budget Lines > Add a line
actions: Click outside the line to finish it.
40.why: The expense side needs its own line.

41.title: Choose the expense position
41.do: In **Budgetary Position**, pick **FY2028 Operating Expenses - Ledger Budget**.
actions: Click the expense position in the list.
41.see: The position name appears in the line.
41.why: This line carries the expense side.

42.title: Line start date
42.why: Same period as the income line.

43.title: Line end date
43.why: Same period as the income line.

44.title: Planned amount: expense
44.why: Expenses are budgeted as a **negative** figure, so that plan and actual are compared in the same direction.

45.title: Save the budget
45.see: The cloud icon disappears. The total shows 70,000,000 (250,000,000 − 180,000,000).
45.why: The budget with both lines is stored.
45.warning: If Odoo says *You have to enter at least a budgetary position or analytic account on a budget line*, there is an empty extra line. Delete it with the bin icon and save again.

46.title: Read the computed columns
points: **Practical Amount** is the posted balance on the position's accounts in the period.
**Theoretical Amount** is the plan spread over the period up to today.
46.see: Practical amounts of 0.0000 (nothing is posted in 2028 yet).
46.why: These columns are filled in by Odoo; you do not type them.

47.title: Confirm the budget
47.why: Only then is the budget treated as an approved plan.
47.tip: Use **Cancel Budget** to take it back.

48.title: Open the Reporting menu
48.do: In the top menu bar, click **Reporting**.
48.why: The comparison of planned against practical amounts is in Reporting.

49.title: Open Budgets Analysis
49.see: The analysis list, grouped by budget. Your new budget is in the list with its planned total.
49.why: It lets you review planned against practical amounts across every budget line.
49.tip: That completes the tour: two positions, one budget with two lines, confirmed and analysed.
